nodes.description: CA8 encodes an enzymatically inactive carbonic-anhydrase-related protein, also called CARP, enriched in cerebellar Purkinje cells. Biochemical experiments show that CARP binds the modulatory region of ITPR1 and reduces its affinity for IP3. Loss of this regulation is a proposed link between CA8 dysfunction and disturbed calcium signaling. Human imaging and whole-embryo zebrafish knockout experiments do not by themselves establish Purkinje-cell-autonomous pathology or the functional effect of each human missense allele.

nodes.description: ATP8A2 is a P4 ATPase that translocates phosphatidylserine from the exoplasmic to the cytosolic membrane leaflet. Disease-associated variants can impair protein folding and abundance or intrinsic phospholipid-activated ATPase activity. These mechanisms require separate assessment: some catalytically inactive variants retain normal abundance, whereas R1147W has reduced abundance with preserved specific ATPase activity. Functional results alone do not establish a monotonic relationship between residual activity and clinical severity.

nodes.description: WDR81 coordinates p62-dependent recognition of ubiquitinated protein aggregates with recruitment of LC3C through its LC3-interacting regions. WDR81 loss impairs this selective aggrephagy function in cultured cells. This function is separable from the WDR91-dependent endosomal role and does not imply failure of general autophagy. Brain-specific Wdr81 knockout causes neuronal p62 accumulation in mice but does not reproduce the gross developmental brain abnormalities of human CAMRQ2; a patient-variant-specific aggrephagy defect remains unestablished.
